name: Toby Diaz
life: “I still remember a birthday my customer remembered and I forgot.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Toby asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I sell drugs and used to think settling money settled everything. One customer asked me to remember a birthday instead.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Toby has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Toby touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To remember the former customer's birthday.
family: Nell Graves is Toby’s half-sibling. Toby chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Nell brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Hem by hem*, Nell says, “I've come to photograph the three waistlines.”
connections: Melanie Nelson. A creditor asking for labor gives the dealer who owes a birthday a different idea of repayment.

reactions.situation: The former fence offers to pay money for something irreplaceable
reactions.response: Toby asks the owner what returning money would and wouldn't settle.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Toby tells the stranger when the next opening is, then stays with the neighbor until their turn comes.

reactions.response: Toby listens first to the account of how it was actually used.
